To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

fish fed a diet containing 40% replacement of fish meal by a mixture of soybean and canola meals, and a 40% replacement in the lipid source from fish oil to canola oil, showed a significantly lower growth rate and feed intake, and a lower lipid digestibility than fish fed a diet with 40% replacement by soybean or canola meal, respectively.

the replacement of 40% of the dietary fish meal protein by a combination of soybean meal and canola meal, and of fish oil by canola oil, does not significantly affect the growth performance of rainbow trout, but that the replacement of fish oil by a combination of canola oil and soybean meal or canola meal significantly decreases growth performance.

the substitution of 40% of dietary fish meal protein with canola meal, soybean meal or a mixture of both, combined with fish oil as the dietary lipid source, did not affect growth, nutrient utilization and hematological parameters in rainbow trout.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of fish oil and fish meal replacement with oilseed meals and oil, respectively, on growth, nutrient digestibility and hematology of rainbow trout.
the use of vegetable protein sources in fish feed and their potential to replace the fish meal protein.
the replacement of fish meal and fish oils in the diet of rainbow trout with plant protein meals and plant oil sources.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of canola meal and canola oil, in combination with soybean meal and soybean oil, in rainbow trout diets can be used at 32% of dietary protein and 20% of dietary lipid inclusion levels, respectively, without inducing negative effects on growth performance, body composition, nutrient digestibility, or blood parameters.

fish meal replacement with oilseed meals and oilseed oil substitution of fish oil in rainbow trout diets can be achieved without significant negative impacts on growth performance, feed utilization, body composition or blood chemistry.
fish meal and fish oils are not essential in rainbow trout diets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the substitution of fish meal with soybean or canola meal in diets containing either fish oil or vegetable oil did not induce significant negative effects on fish growth and health.
the use of vegetable protein and vegetable oil in rainbow trout diets does not affect growth performance and nutrient utilization.

the substitution of fish meal with vegetable meals and fish oil with canola oil in rainbow trout diets can be achieved up to a level of 40% without negative effects on growth or nutrient utilization, and without any negative effects on the health of the fish, as indicated by hematological parameters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of canola meal as a fish meal substitute is possible, but only if the diet contains fish oil.

the inclusion of canola oil in the diet should be limited to 10–15% (of the total diet), as the inclusion of more canola oil in fish feeds negatively affects growth, nutrient utilization and fish health.

the replacement of dietary protein and lipid sources in trout diets can be achieved without compromising fish performance, and that canola oil can be used in diets without compromising growth and health.
